To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cryo-ET structure of the human activated splicing complex in three distinct conformations reveals a flux of components in two key transitions, and that the structures provide a framework for understanding splicing in human cells.
the structure of the human activated Bact complex reveals the conformational changes in key components that are essential for the transition to the catalytically active B* complex.
the structure of human spliceosome in the activated state (Bact) has been determined by cryo-electron microscopy, revealing a complex with a well-formed active center.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the activated spliceosome in human cells and the conformational transitions of this complex.
the structure, function, and regulation of the spliceosome and its components, and the molecular mechanisms of pre-mRNA alternative splicing.

understanding the structure, dynamics, and function of the spliceosome, the macromolecular machine that removes introns and joins exons to produce functional messenger RNA (mRNA) from pre-mRNA in all eukaryotes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study presents the structure of the activated spliceosome in the human system.

the structure of the human spliceosome in three different conformational states has been captured and that this structure allows a detailed understanding of the mechanism of splicing and its regulation.

the Bact complex is an activated spliceosome that is poised for the branching reaction and that the Bact-to-C complex transition is a dynamic process involving the flux of components and conformational changes in the Bact complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a structural basis for how the human spliceosome transitions from the inactive to the active state.
the Bact complex is the most active spliceosome conformation, and it is the first structure to reveal the human NTC in the context of the spliceosome.
the human Bact spliceosome is a highly dynamic complex that undergoes a large-scale conformational change during its maturation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Bact complex is a dynamic assembly that contains multiple conformations, which may be important for its function.
the human B complex is highly dynamic and that its conformational states differ in the relative orientations of Prp8 and U5 and in the position of the U5 snRNA.
the human activated spliceosomes exist in three distinct conformations that represent different stages of the Bact complex.
